messages:
maria: Heads-up — deploying vectorizer to staging shows intermittent KMS Decrypt AccessDenied on pod start. Helm chart creates the SA with the IRSA annotation, but pods sometimes boot before the annotation takes effect. Any quick patterns folks use to make this reliable?

maria: Here
re snippets we
pply via Helm (trimmed):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: vectorizer-svc
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/vectorizer-staging-role
```

maria: And TF used elsewhere to add a grant to the KMS key: 
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "vectorizer_decrypt" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.ml_data.id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.vectorizer.arn
  operations = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
```

cheng: Yep, classic timing issue. Common mitigations we've run across: short-term hacks and longer-term infra changes. Quick list: 
- Ensure SA + annotation exists before any pods are created (create SA as a separate manifest applied first).
- Add an initContainer that waits for creds/sts identity before continuing.
- Make deployment restart after Helm finishes (post-install hook that patches SA and restarts).
- Move the IAM Role into Terraform so grants/ordering are explicit.

cheng: Example initContainer (keeps image tiny, retries until STS works):
```yaml
initContainers:
- name: wait-for-aws-creds
  image: amazon/aws-cli:2.16.7
  command: ["/bin/sh","-c","until aws sts get-caller-identity --output text; do sleep 1; done"]
  env:
    - name: AWS_REGION
      value: us-west-2
```

sam: We shipped a small post-install hook in another chart: it patches the SA annotation and then does a `kubectl rollout restart` on the Deployment. That reduced flakes. Example script we used in the hook: 
```bash
kubectl apply -f templates/serviceaccount.yaml -n staging
kubectl patch sa vectorizer-svc -n staging -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn":"arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/vectorizer-staging-role"}}}'
kubectl rollout restart deploy/vectorizer -n staging
```

sam: downside: cluster RBAC / CI runner needs permission to patch/restart. But low friction if your CI already has cluster edit perms.

maria: Good to know. Our chart currently creates SA as part of the chart and the role is injected by the IRSA helper in a separate helm release, so TF grants that expect a role arn end up referencing an arn that isn't stable in ordering.

cheng: If the role is created outside TF (Helm IRSA), consider changing the KMS grant to reference the role ARN string (computed) and add a small retry/depends in your deploy pipeline, or move role creation into TF. Important: key policy must allow the role — grants alone won't help if key policy denies.

cheng: Example minimal key policy snippet we've used (data source + statement):
```hcl
data "aws_iam_policy_document" "kms_policy_for_vectorizer" {
  statement {
    sid = "AllowVectorizerRoleUse"
    principals { type = "AWS"; identifiers = ["arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/vectorizer-staging-role"] }
    actions = ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"]
    resources = ["*"]
  }
}
```

infra-ci: logs from staging cluster (trimmed):
```
2025-11-02T09:12:01Z vectorizer[init] ERROR KMS Decrypt failed: AccessDenied
2025-11-02T09:12:02Z kubelet: pod vectorizer-5c7b9 not yet assuming IRSA role
2025-11-02T09:12:04Z aws-iam-token: serviceaccount annotation added for vectorizer-svc
2025-11-02T09:12:06Z vectorizer main starting, STS identity not present
```

maria: Thanks. Two follow-ups: (1) Can we add a lightweight initContainer that blocks until STS creds exist as a stopgap? (2) I'll add a post-install hook to patch and restart on staging and monitor for a day. If it still flakes I'll move the role into TF.

sam: Happy to review PR. For the initContainer we used alpine + curl + the EKS projected token path check:
```sh
# init script snippet
set -e
TOKEN=/var/run/secrets/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/token
while [ ! -s "$TOKEN" ] || ! aws sts get-caller-identity >/dev/null 2>&1; do
  sleep 1
done
```

cheng: Also check CloudTrail for KMS:Reject or kms:Decrypt Deny entries — if key policy has explicit denies or missing allow for that principal you'll see it there. CloudTrail helps differentiate "didn't have creds yet" vs "policy denies".

maria: Will do. I'll open a draft PR with both: initContainer + post-install hook (helm) and tag you both for review. I'll include notes about RBAC needed for CI to patch and restart.

oncall-bot: Created ticket INF-3241: "staging vectorizer IRSA race - followup". Linked logs and PR when available.

sam: quick nit: if you move role into TF later, remember to set `depends_on` in the grant resource so TF creates the key policy/grant after the role exists. Works much cleaner for deterministic deploys. :+1:

cheng: SGTM. ping here when PR is up and I'll check CloudTrail policies while you roll it out.
